name: Rent vs Buy Calculator India
seoTitle: Rent vs Buy Calculator India 2026 | Compare Long-Term Cost
shortDescription: Compare renting with buying after loan interest, rent growth, home appreciation, maintenance and investing the down payment.
metaDescription: Compare rent vs buy in India using home price, loan, rent growth, appreciation, ownership costs and investment-return assumptions.
formulaExplanation: Calculates reducing-balance EMI, estimated rent, ownership costs, future home value and the opportunity cost of the down payment.
example: Small changes in appreciation and investment return can reverse the outcome.

faqs.question: Does a positive result mean I should buy?
faqs.answer: No. It only means the entered assumptions favour buying mathematically.

faqs.question: What if I don't know future home appreciation?
faqs.answer: Use a conservative rate for your city; the comparison is most reliable when appreciation and rent-growth assumptions are realistic rather than optimistic.

name: Home Affordability Calculator India
seoTitle: Home Affordability Calculator India 2026 | Income & EMI Check
shortDescription: Estimate an affordable property price from take-home income, existing EMIs, down payment, interest rate and a chosen EMI limit.
metaDescription: Find what home price may fit your budget using income, existing EMIs, down payment, rate, tenure and affordability ratio.
formulaExplanation: Works backward from a chosen EMI-to-income limit, subtracts existing EMIs and converts the remainder into an illustrative loan principal.
example: At Rs 1 lakh take-home, Rs 15,000 existing EMIs and a 40% cap, the home EMI budget is Rs 25,000.

faqs.question: Is this the same as bank eligibility?
faqs.answer: No. Lenders apply their own credit, income, age and policy checks.

faqs.question: What EMI ratio should I use?
faqs.answer: Many lenders cap total EMIs near 40-50% of take-home income, but a lower ratio leaves more room for savings and emergencies.

name: Job Offer Comparison Calculator India
seoTitle: Job Offer Comparison Calculator India | Compare CTC & Value
shortDescription: Compare up to three offers on post-tax in-hand pay, with expected variable pay, provident fund, employer benefits, work costs and joining bonus.
metaDescription: Compare up to three salary offers on post-tax in-hand pay rather than headline CTC, including provident fund, benefits, joining bonus and work costs.
formulaExplanation: Converts variable pay into expected value, runs each offer through the same India income-tax calculation for the selected financial year and regime, then adds benefits and subtracts recurring work costs. Provident fund is reported separately because it reduces in-hand pay but remains the employee's money.
example: A higher CTC can lose once uncertain variable pay, commuting costs and a lower basic-pay percentage are taken into account.

faqs.question: Does this compare offers after income tax?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each offer is run through the same income-tax calculation for the financial year and regime you select, so the figures compared are in-hand rather than headline CTC. HRA exemption and surcharge above Rs 50 lakh are not modelled.

faqs.question: How should I estimate the payout chance for variable pay?
faqs.answer: Use your own or peers' historical payout track record at each company rather than the maximum advertised bonus.

faqs.question: Why does the offer with more in-hand pay sometimes lose on total value?
faqs.answer: A higher basic-pay percentage means more provident fund is deducted from your salary and matched by the employer. That lowers monthly cash but raises retirement saving, which is still your money, so the calculator reports both.

faqs.question: Is the joining bonus counted every year?
faqs.answer: No. It is taxed as salary but carries no provident fund, so it is shown only in the year-one row. The ongoing-year comparison excludes it.

name: Salary Increment Calculator India
seoTitle: Salary Increment Calculator India 2026 | Hike & Monthly Difference
shortDescription: Calculate revised annual salary, monthly gross difference, estimated take-home change and real hike after inflation.
metaDescription: Calculate salary hike percentage, revised salary, estimated monthly gain and inflation-adjusted increment in India.
formulaExplanation: Applies the hike to annual salary, estimates take-home with user-entered ratios and adjusts the nominal hike for inflation.
example: A 20% gross hike may produce a smaller bank-account increase if deductions rise.

faqs.question: Why is take-home increase lower than the hike?
faqs.answer: Tax, PF, variable pay and benefit structure may change.

faqs.question: What is a good real hike after inflation?
faqs.answer: A real hike above 0% means purchasing power grew; compare it with your own cost-of-living trend rather than the headline CPI figure.

name: Bonus Tax Calculator India
seoTitle: Bonus Tax Calculator India 2026 | Estimate Net Bonus
shortDescription: Estimate the post-tax value of a bonus using marginal tax rate, cess and payroll deductions.
metaDescription: Estimate how much annual bonus may remain after marginal income tax, cess and other deductions in India.
formulaExplanation: Uses the entered marginal rate, applies cess to estimated income tax and adds other entered payroll deductions.
example: A Rs 2 lakh bonus at 30% plus 4% cess has an estimated tax impact of Rs 62,400 before other deductions.

faqs.question: Is bonus taxed at a special fixed rate?
faqs.answer: It generally forms part of salary income; actual tax depends on total taxable income and regime.

faqs.question: Can employers deduct TDS on a bonus at a flat rate?
faqs.answer: Employers typically estimate TDS using your projected annual tax slab rather than a fixed bonus rate, so the actual deduction can differ from this estimate.

name: FIRE Calculator India
seoTitle: FIRE Calculator India 2026 | Financial Independence Corpus
shortDescription: Estimate a financial-independence corpus, projected corpus and monthly investment needed from expenses and return assumptions.
metaDescription: Estimate your FIRE number using expenses, withdrawal rate, current corpus, inflation, return and monthly investment.
formulaExplanation: Builds a corpus from expenses divided by withdrawal rate, inflates expenses and projects investments with monthly compounding.
example: Rs 60,000 monthly expenses at a 3.5% withdrawal rate gives a current FIRE number near Rs 2.06 crore.

faqs.question: Is the 4% rule guaranteed in India?
faqs.answer: No. Sustainability depends on returns, inflation, tax, asset mix and retirement length.

faqs.question: Should I use pre-tax or post-tax expenses for the FIRE number?
faqs.answer: Use realistic post-tax annual expenses, since withdrawals from your corpus will also need to cover any tax due on that income.

name: Net Worth Tracker Calculator India
seoTitle: Net Worth Tracker Calculator India | Assets, Loans & Financial Health
shortDescription: Add assets, subtract liabilities and calculate total net worth, liquid net worth and debt-to-asset ratio.
metaDescription: Track personal net worth from cash, investments, property, retirement accounts, loans and other liabilities, plus a liquid net worth and debt-to-asset ratio.
formulaExplanation: Adds entered asset values and subtracts outstanding liabilities. Liquid net worth excludes property and retirement assets.
example: Assets of Rs 79 lakh and liabilities of Rs 35 lakh produce net worth of Rs 44 lakh.

faqs.question: Should property use purchase price or current value?
faqs.answer: Use a conservative current market estimate.

faqs.question: Is a negative net worth unusual early in a career?
faqs.answer: No. Education loans and a new home loan can make net worth low or negative in the early years before assets accumulate.

name: Education Loan EMI & Tax Benefit Calculator India
seoTitle: Education Loan EMI Calculator India 2026 | Section 80E Estimate
targetKeyword: education loan EMI tax benefit calculator India
shortDescription: Calculate education-loan EMI and an illustrative interest-deduction tax impact using user-entered assumptions.
metaDescription: Calculate education loan EMI, total interest and an illustrative Section 80E tax impact in India.
formulaExplanation: Calculates reducing-balance EMI and total interest. The tax output is a simplified illustration, not a filing calculation.
example: Actual annual eligible interest should come from the lender certificate.

faqs.question: Does Section 80E deduct principal?
faqs.answer: The deduction generally concerns eligible interest, subject to applicable law and eligibility.

faqs.question: Is there an upper rupee limit on the Section 80E deduction?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed rupee ceiling on the interest deduction, but eligibility is limited to a specified number of years and applies only to interest, not principal repayment.

name: Rental Yield Calculator India
seoTitle: Rental Yield Calculator India 2026 | Gross & Net Yield
shortDescription: Calculate gross and net rental yield after vacancy, maintenance, property tax and other annual costs.
metaDescription: Calculate rental yield in India from property value, rent, vacancy, maintenance, tax and annual costs.
formulaExplanation: Gross rental yield = monthly rent x 12 / current property value x 100. Net annual rent = monthly rent x (12 - vacancy months) - annual maintenance - annual property tax - other annual costs. Net yield = net annual rent / current property value x 100. The final illustration adds the appreciation assumption to net yield; it does not compound returns or include a sale.
example: For a property valued at Rs 50 lakh with Rs 20,000 monthly rent, one vacant month and Rs 40,000 total annual ownership costs: gross annual rent is Rs 2,40,000, rent after vacancy is Rs 2,20,000 and net annual rent is Rs 1,80,000. Gross yield is 4.8%; net yield is 3.6%. These are illustrative inputs, not a market benchmark.

faqs.question: Should I use purchase price or current value?
faqs.answer: Use current value to compare keeping the property with selling it today. For a historical cost-based calculation, enter your chosen invested-cost figure and label the result accordingly; do not compare results using different denominators as if they were equivalent.

faqs.question: What is a good rental yield?
faqs.answer: There is no universal threshold. Compare verified rents, vacancy, costs and property valuations for similar properties in the same area, then consider tax, financing, liquidity and concentration risk. This tool does not contain a local market-yield dataset.

faqs.question: Does net rental yield include my home-loan EMI?
faqs.answer: No. The net yield deducts only the vacancy and annual cost fields shown. Calculate the loan cash flow separately. An EMI includes principal as well as interest, so it is different from an operating expense.

faqs.question: Can net rental yield be negative?
faqs.answer: Yes. If annual ownership costs exceed rent collected after vacancy, net rent and net yield are negative. Check that all expense inputs are annual figures and that costs have not been counted twice.

faqs.question: Is the appreciation result a guaranteed return?
faqs.answer: No. It adds your price-growth assumption to net rental yield for illustration. It does not model sale timing, reinvestment, transaction costs or an actual investment return.

howToUse: Enter a realistic current property value and the monthly rent you expect to collect.
Enter expected vacant months over a year, including any gap between tenants.
Add annual maintenance, property tax and other recurring costs once each.
Read net yield alongside gross yield, then repeat with more vacancy or higher costs.
Treat appreciation as a separate assumption. Compare loan costs and tax separately before deciding whether to keep or sell.
assumptions: Rent and recurring expenses are constant during the modelled year; partial vacancy months reduce rent proportionately.
Property value must be positive. This tool uses the value you enter and does not obtain a valuation or local rental quote.
Net yield here is before personal income tax and financing costs. EMI, loan interest, purchase stamp duty, registration, sale costs and capital-gains tax are not deducted automatically.
Yield plus appreciation is a simple illustration, not a forecast, an IRR or cash you can spend. Property prices can fall.
commonMistakes: Mixing monthly rent with annual expense figures.
Counting the same maintenance bill under both annual maintenance and other costs.
Calling gross yield take-home income, or ignoring vacant months.
Comparing a pre-tax, unlevered property yield with an after-tax or leveraged investment return.

contentSections.heading: How one extra vacant month changes net yield
contentSections.body: Using the worked example, a second vacant month lowers rent after vacancy from Rs 2,20,000 to Rs 2,00,000. With the same Rs 40,000 costs, net rent becomes Rs 1,60,000 and net yield falls from 3.6% to 3.2%. This isolates vacancy risk; it does not assume that rent or property value will stay unchanged.

contentSections.heading: Using yield for a hold-or-sell comparison
contentSections.body: Current value answers what the rental cash flow earns on the property value today. Your original purchase cost answers a different question about your invested cost. Use a consistent denominator for comparisons, and separately account for sale costs, taxes, loan balance and the income you would give up. A high yield alone does not establish that a property is a good investment.

name: Debt Snowball Calculator India
seoTitle: Debt Snowball Calculator India | Payoff Order & Time
shortDescription: Estimate payoff time for three debts as extra money rolls from the smallest balance to the next debt.
metaDescription: Plan a debt snowball using three balances, rates, minimum payments and an extra monthly payment.
formulaExplanation: For each debt, estimated months = -log(1 - balance × monthly rate / payment) / log(1 + monthly rate). The monthly rate is the annual percentage rate divided by 1,200. Extra payment goes to debt 1, then its cleared minimum payment rolls into debt 2, and both cleared payments roll into debt 3. The calculator adds these stage estimates using each debt's original balance; it does not reduce later balances by minimum payments made during earlier stages. The total is therefore an approximation, not a month-by-month repayment schedule. A payment must exceed monthly interest for the balance to fall.
example: Enter debts of ₹50,000 at 18%, ₹1,50,000 at 14% and ₹4,00,000 at 11%, with minimum payments of ₹3,000, ₹5,000 and ₹9,000, plus ₹5,000 extra each month. Total debt is ₹6,00,000 and the starting monthly payment is ₹22,000. Stage payments are ₹8,000, ₹13,000 and ₹22,000, giving about 6.6, 12.5 and 20.0 months respectively, or 39.1 months in this model. The total uses original balances at each stage; an actual schedule that credits ongoing minimum payments to later debts can finish sooner.

faqs.question: Should debts be entered by balance or rate?
faqs.answer: For snowball, enter smallest balance first. Avalanche prioritises highest rate.

faqs.question: Does the snowball method minimise total interest paid?
faqs.answer: Not always. Paying the highest-interest debt first (avalanche method) usually saves more interest; snowball prioritises quick wins for motivation instead.
